test: Test 6: colour as an identity cue for objects, enlarged object neighbourhoods and groups
written: 2026-10-19, before color_extract.py / test6.py were written or run
extraction: One pass over each robot's L515 colour stream; for every saved FastSAM detection (pts_img = mask pixel mean, covs_img = mask pixel covariance) the mean RGB is computed inside the ellipse given by Mahalanobis distance m. No depth-based trimming anywhere.

weightings.full: uniform over m <= 2 (approximately the whole segment, including neighbours inside merged segments)

object_level.data: 798 annotated pairs; 314 same_object vs 341 different_objects; each side's colour = median over its annotated views
object_level.neighbourhood_colour: area-weighted mean colour of all detections of the same frame whose camera-frame 3D centroid lies within 0.7 m of the side's detection (the detection itself included)
object_level.metric: AUC of -distance for same vs different; 95% bootstrap interval over the 24 episodes; also on gate-rejected pairs; size similarity s of hypothesis 6 (AUC 0.658) as the reference
object_level.rule: colour is a stronger identity cue than size if AUC >= 0.75 and the lower bootstrap bound exceeds 0.66

group_level.groups: oracle: for robot r at step k, detections of r in the last 20 s whose world position (GT body pose x T_BC) is within 0.5 m XY of a box of GT group g and 0.08 <= z < 0.9 m; at least 3 detections

signatures.set: symmetric Chamfer distance between member colour sets

group_level.metrics: as test 3: top-1, chance, top-2 recall, AUC; colour alone and colour plus test-3 size/arrangement (equal weights after median normalisation)
group_level.rule: as test 3: top-1 >= 0.80 and top-2 recall >= 0.95 -> proceed to on-board group matching by colour

status: exploratory; one recording; four robots with independent auto exposure / white balance
